summary: The Association Health Plans Act amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to clarify how certain groups or associations of employers can sponsor group health plans. The bill sets specific criteria for these associations to be treated as single employers, outlines requirements for self-employed individuals to participate, and establishes rules for how these plans set premium rates and handle non-discrimination protections.

affected_groups.effect: Can form or join associations to sponsor group health plans for their employees, with contribution rates adjusted based on their specific risk profile.
May participate in association health plans as both an employer and an employee, provided they meet minimum work-hour and income criteria and are monitored by the association board.
Receive health coverage through association plans that are subject to federal consumer protections like pre-existing condition bans and health-status non-discrimination rules.

key_provisions: Allows a group or association of employers to be treated as an employer to sponsor a group health plan, regardless of whether the employers are in the same industry, trade, or profession, provided specific criteria are met.

Requires the association plan to provide coverage to at least 51 employees after aggregating all employees of member employers, and requires the association to have been actively in existence for at least two years.
Establishes a governing board for the association plan where at least 75 percent of the board members are participating employer members elected by each participating employer casting one vote.

Permits self-employed individuals to qualify as both an employer member and an employee participant in the association plan, subject to specific work-hour and income requirements monitored by the association board.

Allows association health plans to establish base premium rates using a modified community rating methodology based on pooled claims, and to adjust contribution rates for individual employer members based on their specific risk profiles.
Mandates that plans consisting solely of self-employed individuals must treat all members as a single risk pool, pool all claims, and charge each participant the same premium rate.
Prohibits association health plans from discriminating on eligibility or premium amounts based on health status-related factors, and bans denying coverage based on pre-existing conditions.
missing_information: The bill does not specify numerical impact estimates regarding how many individuals or employers are expected to join these association health plans.
The bill does not provide financial data regarding the change in federal revenue or administrative costs.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Association Health Plans Act amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) to clarify how certain groups or associations of employers can sponsor group health plans. The bill sets specific criteria for these associations to be treated as single employers, outlines requirements for self-employed individuals to participate, and establishes rules for how these plans set premium rates and handle non-discrimination protections.
summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts federal labor and health benefit laws by defining the legal and operational standards for association health plans under ERISA, affecting how employers and self-employed individuals pool together to purchase health insurance coverage.
